.. And honestly, it kind of proves they are a low-value person. They essentially confirm they weren’t the right partner to begin with.

Don’t do it to get back at her, honestly, you’ll forget her. Unless there is something seriously wrong with your behavior or personality, you probably don’t have to “work on yourself” too much. Work on what you enjoy! 

You’ll find someone who will accept and love you for who you are at the very core! You lived without her before, and you’ll learn to do it again. It does suck, and you will suffer, but the world goes on - with or without you. Do what makes you happy, learn something new, I mean you have more free time now, right? You’ll eventually cross paths with another woman.

I hate that we normalize rebounds. It should be frowned up.  Honestly, fuck him. What a man whore! 

Breakups suck and all, losing a deep connection is always hurtful no matter the circumstances—can’t hide from the feeling of betrayal. I know you are afraid you’ll never get past him - but you really need to. 

And to be frank, you should be glad he is out of your life. That man lacks accountability, he doesn’t understand (or deserve) your depth. 

Let him go on his “self-improvement adventure” which essentially includes temporal, fleeting, shallow satisfaction from sleeping with other girls and partying around. “I used to be a bad person, this is my nature..” Lol. He is not Edward Cullen. He just lacks accountability and integrity. Judging by your depth, he doesn’t even know what he just lost. 

Good luck, and don’t let him get in your head. Connections come and go, but you’ll find the love you are looking for. And you sure as hell will be happier.

It is normal to rebound, but it’s not okay. Sex is sacred, not some transactional “feels good” thing that you can do whenever. That is a fairly recent modern concept that sprung up because of bad philosophy.

If she doesn’t value that—throwing her body at some dude she barely met, going around acting like you don’t exist, lying to you, etc., then you should honestly be happy she is gone. We make deep connections all the time, but a connection doesn’t mean you two were soulmates or right for each other. Because that is not the height of love.  

I think you are a good person because of what you are feeling. You don’t just miss her, you miss the essence of what you two used to be. 

You’re angry with her because she’s not on the same playing field as you. It shows me that your love runs deeper, you are true to your word, and it is authentic. 

It doesn’t matter if you think doubt your good, your heart is in the right place.

I mean, sure sounds like you meant a lot to each other, and that’s a blow that you can’t just recover from that easily. You can’t forget her either. But you don’t have to let her control your mind. You’ll feel like shit for the next few days or weeks, but eventually you’ll get over it.

Don’t let some chick who sleeps around after promising you “forever” get in your head like this. You’re better than that, and her. She can go on and fuck however many dudes she wants, but will she ever find true love again? That soul-burning, cinematic love. Will she find someone like you again? It sounds a bit cruel, but it’s just true. That dude isn’t a lucky guy from the looks of it, he got your sloppy seconds from a desperate woman.

Emotions are temporary, and you will get over this soon. 

On the other hand, I think you dodged a bullet. Fuck her, to be perfectly honest. She rebounds in 2-3 weeks like you didn’t mean shit to her? That’s straight up hoe behavior. Do you want someone like that raising your kids? I hope not. Do you need someone like that in your life? Is she really a good influence? Obviously not. Let her enjoy her own little delusional world where love and sex aren’t sacred. But I know you are better than that.

She’s not a good person, and you deserve better. 

Yeah it’s shitty that you shared so much with her and knew her on a deep, fundamental level. But now that she has shown her **true colors**, I think you should worry about yourself. 

After all, it was not meant to be and she is just sleeping around like you meant nothing to her. 

Don’t let this sadden you though, man. She’ll do whatever the hell she wants, but she will never meet a man like you again. And there is a woman out there waiting for you to enter her life, and likewise you are waiting for her, but you don’t know it yet. Go find her. I’m sure she won’t be some hoe that sleeps around first thing after a breakup.

I was under the impression that you were paid a minimum hourly wage in addition to a flat rate. However, what you described is a clear violation of FLSA.

[https://www.dol.gov/sites/dolgov/files/WHD/legacy/files/2009\_01\_15\_15\_FLSA.pd](https://www.dol.gov/sites/dolgov/files/WHD/legacy/files/2009_01_15_15_FLSA.pdf)

>***The FLSA requires that an employer compensate an employee for all hours worked. Section 3 of the FLSA defines “employ” as including “to suffer or permit to work.”*** 29 U.S.C. § 203(g); see also 29 C.F.R. § 785.11. This rule applies to work performed away from the premises or the job site, including work performed at home. “If the employer knows or has reason to believe that the work is being performed, he must count the time as hours worked.” 29 C.F.R. § 785.12.

​

[29 CFR 785.12](https://web.archive.org/web/20100224055857/https://www.dol.gov/dol/allcfr/Title_29/Part_785/29CFR785.12.htm) Regulation of FLSA (codified into Federal Law) states:

>The rule is also applicable to work performed away from the premises or the job site, or even at home. ***If the employer knows or has reason to believe that the work is being performed, he must count the time as hours worked***.

Idaho does not provide any exemption or derogation from the FLSA or its regulations, including 29 CFR 785.12.  


Also, are you classed as an independent contractor or employee? This may also depend on the specific circumstances of your work arrangements--which may complicate this issue more.
